current.title: The Amazon Has Lost 750,000 Square Kilometers Since 1970
current.hook: The clearing is dropping. The damage isn't.
current.closing: Fewer trees fall each year. The bill still grows.
current.question: Would you give up beef to save the rainforest? Tell me below.

segments.say: In 2004 Brazil cleared 27,772 square kilometers of Amazon rainforest in one year. By 2024 that had fallen all the way to 6,288 -- the lowest in almost a decade.
But add up every year since 1970, and the Amazon has lost about 750,000 square kilometers total -- an area bigger than the whole country of France.
So where does all that cleared land go? Close to 80 percent becomes cattle pasture. Almost every acre lost boils down to the world's demand for beef.

problems: seg4 holds one frame from 40.22s to 45.50s — four empty tiles, a dim '4 times over', and a mascot that only wiggles an arm; the video ends on a freeze.
seg4's tiles are empty containers, so the '4 times over' payoff is a label claiming something the picture never shows.
Captions are drawn over chart labels: 'The clearing'/'The damage' sit on the 2004 row at hook@0.8 and seg0:mid, cutting '27772' down to '7772' and covering the year.
At seg1:start Data stands on top of the 27772 value, and at seg1:mid/end his arm crosses the '27772' end-label of the range dial.
A teal ellipse is stroked straight through '699,173 left of 750,000' at seg2:mid.
The seg2 bucket drains from 750,000 downward, reading as forest left rather than forest lost — the metaphor contradicts the narration.
fixes: Re-time seg4 so the four tiles land one per beat across the full 5s and the last tile seats on the final word; never let the closing composition reach its end state before the audio does.
Fill seg4's tiles with the subject — cleared-land blocks, cattle, tree stumps — so a viewer counts four without reading '4 times over', and lift that label to ink contrast.
Reserve a caption band clear of the chart plot: push narration captions to the lower safe area for seg0/hook instead of drawing them across the 2004 row.
Move Data off the value column at seg1:start and off the dial's end-label at seg1:mid — place him clear of any text extent, measured, not eyeballed.
Kill the ellipse prop crossing the counter at seg2:mid, or move the counter above it.
Flip seg2's vessel: fill it as the loss accumulates to 750,000 rather than draining from it, so the picture and the narration agree.

rules: TITLE or HOOK must contain a consequential NUMBER from the data below (the gate refuses a title+hook with no digit in either).

TITLE must be a PREMISE, not a searchable noun phrase: more than five words, or a number, or a question mark, or a tension word. 'Oldest Written Languages' is the failure; 'Why 3 of the 5 Oldest Scripts Are Still Unreadable' is the shape.

Every segment's TOPIC (a 2-4 word on-screen label) must share at least one real word with the TITLE — the gate checks a keyword bridge from each segment to the headline. Rename the topic, or write the title so it names what the segments are about.

Every NUMBER you say in a segment's SAY must be one that segment's data can show: a listed value, a difference between two of them, a percent change, a share of the total, or the same value in a bigger unit. A number from nowhere is refused — a guard derives every spoken quantity from the listed points.
Keep every number that is already correct. Do not add a country, company or person the data does not name.
Each SAY is one spoken sentence or two, at most 40 words, and says its beat's headline number out loud.
TOPIC labels are printed on the video: at most 4 words, no clause.
